facts.statement: Tonganosaurus is a mamenchisaurid sauropod dinosaur named after the town of Tong'an in Sichuan, China, and is similar to Omeisaurus.
facts.quote: Tonganosaurus (named for the town of Tong'an, Sichuan where it was found) is a genus of mamenchisaurid sauropod dinosaur, similar to Omeisaurus.

facts.statement: The ratio of the front limb length to the rear limb length in Tonganosaurus is 0.80.
facts.quote: The ratio of the front and rear limbs is 0.80.

facts.statement: The tibia of Tonganosaurus was straight and thick, measuring 75% of the length of the femur.
facts.quote: The tibia was straight and thick, with a length 75% that of the femur.

facts.statement: Based on comparisons with Omeisaurus, the skeleton of Tonganosaurus is calculated to be 11.6 meters long, with an estimated living length of about 12 meters.
facts.quote: The skeleton of Tonganosaurus has been calculated in size, using Omeisaurus as reference, at 11.6 m long. In life, it was probably a little bigger, about 12 m.

facts.statement: Tonganosaurus was first named by Li Kui, Yang Chun-Yan, Liu Jian, and Wang Zheng-Xin in 2010, with the type species designated as Tonganosaurus hei.
facts.quote: It was first named by Li Kui, Yang Chun-Yan, Liu Jian, and Wang Zheng-Xin in 2010, and the type species is Tonganosaurus hei.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Tonganosaurus is housed at the Chengdu University of Technology Museum under the catalog number MCDUT 14454.
facts.quote: The specimen was kept at Chengdu University of Technology Museum, with the number MCDUT 14454.

facts.statement: Tonganosaurus is the oldest known member of the mamenchisaurid family, existing almost 15 million years before the next-oldest members of the group.
facts.quote: Tonganosaurus is the oldest known member of the mamenchisaurids, being almost 15 million years older than the next-oldest members of the group.

facts.statement: Tonganosaurus is believed to date from the late Early Jurassic (Pliensbachian) based on the Yimen Formation where it was found.
facts.quote: The formation has been divided into three levels, and Tonganosaurus appears to be of late Early Jurassic (Pliensbachian) in age.

facts.statement: Tonganosaurus lived during the Early Jurassic, approximately 184.5 million years ago, in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: que vivió a principios del período Jurásico, hace aproximadamente 184,5 millones de años, en el Pliensbachiense, en lo que hoy es Asia.

facts.statement: The holotype of Tonganosaurus is associated with Brontopodus footprints that may have been made by this taxon, suggesting it left such tracks.
facts.quote: Tonganosaurus holotype comes from the Upper section of the Yimen Formation, being associated with Brontopodus tracks with also Mamenchisaurid resemblance, that maybe were made by this taxon.

facts.statement: The plant fossils found with Tonganosaurus, dominated by the genus Aclistochara, suggest it lived in shallow-to-deep lake and flood environments.
facts.quote: The Stonewort assemblage is dominated by the genus Aclistochara (A. nuguishanensis, A. yunnanensis) associated with elements of Porochara and sporadic individuals of Stenochara, suggesting shallow-deep lake and flood environments.

facts.statement: Tonganosaurus is classified within the family Mamenchisauridae.
The genus Tonganosaurus was established by Li et al. in 2010.
The specific horizon of the specimen and the precise age of the Yimen Formation remain controversial among researchers.
facts.quote: The horizon of the specimen and the age of the Yimen Formation is controversial.
